findings.claim: The analysis identifies the both-providers-enabled panic mode but provides no re-evaluation trigger or verification guard against feature unification reintroducing it from another workspace crate depending on jsonwebtoken 11 with rust_crypto.
findings.evidence: The artifact states the pinned source 'selects a built-in only when exactly one provider feature is enabled. Neither or both returns a provider whose operations panic,' yet the 'Re-evaluation triggers' list and the 'Parent A0 handoff' contain no check that exactly one provider feature stays active across the workspace. Cargo features are additive, and the file tree shows many workspace manifests (crates/prometheus-skill-system, tools/uar-jwt-proxy, sdks/rust, src-tauri) that could later add a jsonwebtoken 11 dependency with rust_crypto, silently flipping the runtime back to panicking while cargo check/clippy still pass.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a re-evaluation trigger ('any other workspace member enables a provider feature on jsonwebtoken 11') and a CI/handoff check such as `cargo tree --locked --features server-full -e features -i jsonwebtoken@11.0.0` asserting exactly one of aws_lc_rs/rust_crypto is active.

findings.claim: Handoff step 8 references 'all six parent changes' and 'the pinned Tier 2 command,' neither of which is defined anywhere in this artifact, while the handoff itself lists eight numbered steps.
findings.evidence: "8. Do not run the pinned Tier 2 command until all six parent changes reach phase completion." The preceding 'Parent A0 handoff' enumerates items 1 through 8, mixing manifest edits, test additions, and commands, so the plan stage cannot determine which six items constitute the 'six parent changes' or what the Tier 2 command is without the parent contract.
findings.suggested_fix: Enumerate the six parent changes by reference to specific handoff items, and quote or fully identify the pinned Tier 2 command inline so the plan stage can sequence work without external documents.

findings.claim: The dismissal of downgrading to jsonwebtoken 10 is asserted without evidence even though 10.4.0 is already active transitively and the assess handoff named 'jwt-version-standard-unresolved' as a gap to resolve.
findings.evidence: "Version 11 remains the maintained direct API line; downgrading would not solve a requirement and would discard the current provider abstraction." No tier evidence (e.g., a cargo info result, upstream release note, or maintenance check for the 10.x line) is cited for this claim in analysis.md or library-candidates.json, and aligning with the already-locked 10.4.0 would also remove a duplicate major version from the graph — an argument the artifact never weighs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one evidence entry (tier 1 or 3) covering jsonwebtoken 10.x maintenance status and whether it ships a default crypto backend, so the version-standard gap is resolved by evidence rather than assertion.
